h1: The 4 Best Room Dividers on Wheels of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Room Dividers on Wheels: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 4 best room dividers on wheels with confirmed casters, compared on height, width, panel count and price bucket.
summary: The SUNALLY 6FT 4-Panel is our top rolling divider, with lockable wheels, 6 ft height and 88 in width. The black 6FT 4-Panel is a close twin, the Kokorona is the widest at 119 in, and the VAMFUTRE single panel is the cheap one with brakes.
intro: Many dividers sold as rolling screens never actually list wheels. Searching for room dividers on wheels returns plenty of plain freestanding panels, and you only find out after unboxing that the screen has to be carried.
We kept only four dividers whose listings confirm wheels or casters, and dropped the ones that do not. Rankings use width, height, panel count and whether wheels lock or have brakes.

products.name: SUNALLY 6FT Folding Privacy Screen with Lockable Wheels (4 Panel)
products.verdict: Lockable wheels on a 6 ft fabric screen that needs no drilling.
products.description:
The SUNALLY is a 4-panel fabric folding screen, 6 ft tall and 88 in wide, with lockable wheels confirmed in the listing. It stands freely with no drilling.

It ranks first because it states both its dimensions and its lockable wheels, which matters when you reposition it room to room. It is narrower than the Kokorona. It costs $50-100.

Best for flexible room splitting. The caveat is that 88 in will not span very wide openings.
products.skipIf: You need to span a very wide opening.

products.name: 6FT 4-Panel Folding Privacy Screen with Lockable Wheels, Black
products.verdict: Nearly the same screen in a black finish.
products.description:
This is a 6 ft 4-panel fabric folding screen in black with lockable wheels, and it needs no drilling. Its price falls between $50 and $100.

Second place fits, since the listing never states a width the way the SUNALLY does. Choose it for the black finish. The tradeoff is the missing width figure.

Best for black-themed rooms. The caveat is you should confirm the width before ordering.
products.idealFor: Rooms where black suits the decor.
products.skipIf: You need the width stated up front.

products.name: Kokorona 6 Panel Rolling Privacy Screen with Lockable Wheels (119 in W x 70 in H)
products.verdict: The widest rolling divider here at 119 in.
products.description:
The Kokorona is a 6-panel rolling screen, 119 in wide and 70 in tall, with lockable wheels and cover strips included. It is freestanding.

It ranks third because it costs more at $100-200 and is a bit shorter than the 6 ft models, though it spans the most floor. The tradeoff is price and height.

Best for wide openings and open-plan spaces. The caveat is that it is the most expensive pick.
products.skipIf: You want a taller 6 ft screen.

products.name: VAMFUTRE 6FT Single Panel Room Divider with Caster Wheels & Brakes
products.verdict: A simple single panel with caster wheels and brakes.
products.description:
The VAMFUTRE is a single-panel divider, approximately 6 ft tall, with caster wheels and brakes confirmed, and it is freestanding. It costs $25-50.

It ranks last because one panel covers far less than a folding screen. It is the cheapest here and has brakes. The tradeoff is coverage.

Best for a small corner or a doorway. The caveat is that the height is listed as approximate.
products.skipIf: You need to divide a large space.

whatMatters.detail: Many dividers look like they roll but do not. A listing must say wheels or casters. Look for the word in the title or bullets.
A screen without locks can drift when bumped. Locks keep it where you set it. Check for lockable wheels or brakes.
Width sets how much opening a screen can span. Folding screens can be set at angles. Check the width in inches.
A 6 ft screen gives more privacy than 70 in. Taller models also look more like walls. Check the height in the listing.
More panels spread wider and fold smaller. A single panel is simple but covers little. Check the number of panels.

faq.q: Do all room dividers have wheels?
faq.a: No. Many are plain freestanding panels. We included only four with wheels confirmed in the listing.
Assuming a screen rolls. Always check the listing for wheels or casters.

faq.q: Is the Kokorona worth more than the SUNALLY?
faq.a: If you need 119 in of width, yes. Otherwise the SUNALLY is taller and cheaper.
No. All four are freestanding and listed as no drilling.

faq.q: How do I keep it from rolling?
faq.a: Engage the wheel locks or brakes. The VAMFUTRE lists brakes, and the others list lockable wheels.
Several, like the Amsleekey and RANTILA, do not confirm wheels.

finalTake: The SUNALLY 4-panel is the best rolling room divider here, thanks to confirmed lockable wheels and clear dimensions. The Kokorona is the widest, the black 6FT is a close twin and the VAMFUTRE is the budget buy. Always confirm wheels before ordering.
